question: policy summary
answer: Schema-derived. Drop position = dropPoint(doc, pos, slice): walk from the pointer depth up to doc and take the first depth whose content expression accepts the slice (canReplace), else a second pass that allows one wrapping (findWrapping); no depth cap, no per-container policy, isolating is ignored.

question: Q1 drop target source
answer: Schema content model. handleDrop calls dropPoint and falls back to the raw pointer pos when it returns null, then replaceRangeWith/replaceRange (Fitter) commits; plugins can override everything through the handleDrop prop.

question: Q2 drop inside containers
answer: Yes wherever the schema allows: table cell (cell content block+), blockquote, list item, details all accept a block slice; dropPoint does not read isolating, so cell boundaries do not stop a drop (only replace/delete/lift consult isolating).

question: Q3 draggable nodes
answer: NodeSpec.draggable (default false) lets a node be dragged without being selected; mousedown arms mightDrag only if draggable and selectable!==false, or if a NodeSelection already covers it; any non-empty selection is draggable natively. No drag handle in core.

question: Q4 per-container restriction
answer: None beyond the schema. A tableRow slice fits only where a table accepts rows, but dropPoint accepts any table (not the source table). disableDropCursor on a NodeSpec only hides the cursor; it does not block the drop.

question: Q5 hover indicator and cost
answer: prosemirror-dropcursor on every dragover (no throttle): posAtCoords, optional disableDropCursor, dropPoint (O(depth) canReplace, up to 2 passes), then 1-2 getBoundingClientRect reads on neighbor nodes; indicator always equals what the default drop would do.

question: policy summary
answer: Drag source = DragHandle extension (top-level by default, or rule-scored nested candidates); drop target = unmodified ProseMirror dropPoint plus prosemirror-dropcursor, so landing is schema-derived.

question: Q1 drop target source
answer: Schema (ProseMirror default). The drag handle only sets view.dragging={slice, move:true, node}; core Drop extension's handleDrop only emits an event and returns undefined, so PM handleDrop/dropPoint decides.

question: Q2 drop inside containers
answer: Yes, per schema: tableCell/tableHeader/details are isolating but dropPoint ignores isolating, so a dragged top-level block can land inside cells, list items, blockquotes, details content (inferred from dropPoint + content exprs, not run).

question: Q3 draggable nodes
answer: Default nested:false: handle targets the doc child under the pointer (findClosestTopLevelBlock / getOuterNode) and drags a depth-0 NodeRangeSelection. nested:true: candidates = every ancestor depth plus a block atom at nodeAfter, score 1000 minus rule deductions (>=1000 excludes), edge detection near left edge prefers parents; default rules exclude first child of listItem/taskItem, list wrappers, tableRow/tableCell/tableHeader and header content, inline nodes; allowedContainers whitelist. Separately NodeSpec draggable (image, audio, youtube) with [data-drag-handle] in NodeViews.

question: Q4 per-container restriction
answer: Source side only: tableStructure rule says row/cell dragging belongs to table extensions; no target-side rule, so no rows-stay-in-table or columns-stay-in-group logic in the drag handle.

question: Q5 hover indicator and cost
answer: Handle: mousemove coalesced to one requestAnimationFrame; non-nested = elementsFromPoint + parent walk; nested = posAtCoords + rules per depth + nodeDOM + getBoundingClientRect per candidate (edge detection), O(depth). Drop indicator = prosemirror-dropcursor per dragover (see ProseMirror).

question: policy summary
answer: Schema-derived via ProseMirror dropPoint over a block-structured schema (doc > blockGroup > blockContainer(blockContent, blockGroup?)), plus plugin policy: multi-column edge drops (handleDrop + computeDropPosition hook) and a separate same-table row/column DnD.

question: Q1 drop target source
answer: Schema: slice of blockContainer nodes, PM default drop runs dropPoint, which only fits blockContainer into blockGroup or column; cross-editor drags rebuild view.dragging from blocknote/html so PM still drops between blocks. computeDropPosition hook may move or veto only the indicator; actual edge drop is a separate handleDrop plugin.

question: Q2 drop inside containers
answer: Into any existing children list (nested blockGroup, i.e. indented children, toggle children) and into columns (column content blockContainer+). Not into table cells (tableParagraph content inline*). Pointer inside a childless block lands as a sibling: pass 1 finds the outer blockGroup before pass 2 could wrap in a new blockGroup (inferred from dropPoint order).

question: Q3 draggable nodes
answer: Every blockContainer at any depth: hover climbs DOM to data-node-type=blockContainer, then re-probes at the reference block's right edge to pick the innermost nested block; inside columnList it shifts x by +50px. column/columnList are never handle targets. Drag = NodeSelection of the block, or MultipleNodeSelection when the selection spans blocks.

question: Q4 per-container restriction
answer: Table rows/columns: TableHandles clamps the pointer to the source table rect, moves by index inside that table, and canRowBeDraggedInto/canColumnBeDraggedInto refuse targets that would split merged cells. Columns: edge drop (left edge or right 10%) creates a columnList or inserts a new column with width normalization; dropping a column's whole content on its own edge is a no-op.

question: Q5 hover indicator and cost
answer: Side menu mousemove (unthrottled): editor rect + 2x elementsFromPoint + 1 rect. Dragover: custom DropCursor = posAtCoords + dropPoint + optional hook (multi-column adds posAtCoords + nodeDOM rect); document-level dragover also querySelectorAll('.bn-editor') + rect per editor for cross-editor routing.

question: policy summary
answer: Hard-coded depth: DraggableBlockPlugin_EXPERIMENTAL only reorders root children; drop = insertBefore/insertAfter of the nearest root child by pointer Y, no schema or node policy.

question: Q1 drop target source
answer: Hard-coded top level: getBlockElement scans $getRoot().getChildrenKeys() rects; DROP_COMMAND handler inserts the dragged node before/after that root child by comparing pageY to its top.

question: Q2 drop inside containers
answer: No. Only root siblings; a drop over a quote, list item or table cell lands before/after the whole top-level node.

question: Q3 draggable nodes
answer: Every root child (whole list, whole table, whole quote); handle stores the node key in application/x-lexical-drag-block. No per-node draggable flag in core; images use their own DRAGSTART/DROP handling in the playground.

question: Q4 per-container restriction
answer: Playground only (not the package): TableHoverActionsV2 column reorder via Pragmatic DnD; drop target canDrop requires same tableKey and $isSimpleTable, so columns stay in their table.

question: Q5 hover indicator and cost
answer: Unthrottled mousemove/dragover: copy root children keys (O(n)) then walk from the last hit index in the pointer direction, each step getBoundingClientRect + 3 getComputedStyle (collapsed margins); amortized small, O(n) on jumps. Target line drawn at block edge.

question: policy summary
answer: Geometry first, schema at commit: prosemirror-drop-indicator lists the before/after boundary of every block (excluding textblock content) as candidates, picks the nearest by distance, filters with composable onDrag vetoes (list, table handle), and its handleDrop commits through replaceRangeWith/replaceRange, which repairs schema-invalid points.

question: Q1 drop target source
answer: Per-plugin policy over geometric candidates; no dropPoint or canReplace at hover. Commit uses replaceRangeWith (insertPoint walks outward to a valid parent) or replaceRange (Fitter wraps/closes); a no-op insert is swallowed (returns true).

question: Q2 drop inside containers
answer: Yes: candidates exist inside every non-textblock block (blockquote, flat list, table rows and cells). Outcome for schema-invalid spots such as between table cells depends on insertPoint/Fitter, likely moving outside the table (inferred, not run).

question: Q3 draggable nodes
answer: Block handle: binary-search descent by Y through the doc, stopping at the first textblock, atom or isolating node (so a table is one unit); if that node is the first child of a non-doc parent (list, blockquote), the handle targets the parent. NodeSpec.draggable is not consulted. Drag = NodeSelection + clipboard serialization.

question: Q4 per-container restriction
answer: list onDrag veto: a list node may not drop as first child of another list. Table rows/columns: table-handle drags carry application/x-prosekit-table-handle-drag (block indicator hides) and drop calls moveTableRow/moveTableColumn by index on the table at the selection, so rows stay in their table.

question: Q5 hover indicator and cost
answer: Target list cached while doc identity and editor rect are unchanged, else rebuilt with one getBoundingClientRect per block (O(N) layout reads). Each dragover with new coords sorts all 2N candidates by Manhattan distance (O(N log N)), keeps the top 8, runs onDrag vetoes. The 'dragging onto itself' check discards the target instead of trying the next one. Handle hover: pointermove throttled 200ms, O(depth x log children) rect reads.

question: policy summary
answer: No block DnD. Native contenteditable drag of the selection or a void; drop = caret range under the pointer, delete source range, insertData/insertFragment at that point; normalization repairs structure.

question: Q1 drop target source
answer: Caret position from caretRangeFromPoint/caretPositionFromPoint (findEventRange); over a void it snaps before/after by nearest edge. No schema or depth check before insertion.

question: Q2 drop inside containers
answer: Anywhere a caret can land, including table cells, quotes and list items; a block fragment is merged/split into the target block by insertFragment rather than placed between blocks.

question: Q3 draggable nodes
answer: No drag handle or draggable flag; dragstart over a void element selects that void so its fragment is dragged; otherwise the text selection.

question: Q4 per-container restriction
answer: None in core; left to user onDrop handlers and normalizeNode.

question: Q5 hover indicator and cost
answer: No custom indicator; browser caret. dragover only maps target DOM to a Slate node and preventDefaults over voids (O(1) WeakMap lookups).

question: policy summary
answer: Schema-flag driven: in block mode the target is before/after the closest model element with schema isBlock, or a binary-searched child of a container that accepts $block; insertion goes through the clipboard pipeline's schema-checked insertContent, and the source is only deleted if insertion succeeded.

question: Q1 drop target source
answer: Schema (isBlock, checkChild $block/$text) plus geometry (before/after by vertical midpoint). Non-block mode checks checkChild for each dragged item at the text position. canEditAt and 'target inside dragged range' veto the marker.

question: Q2 drop inside containers
answer: Yes: tableCell allowContentOf $container and blockQuote inherits $container, so the closest isBlock paragraph inside a cell or quote becomes the anchor and the drop lands inside that container; disallowed content makes insertContent fail and the move is cancelled.

question: Q3 draggable nodes
answer: Widgets (isWidget, via selection handle or direct hit, not nested editables) and selected blocks: DragDropBlockToolbar makes the BlockToolbar button draggable and drags selection.getSelectedBlocks() (isBlock elements not nested in other blocks), offsetting clientX by 100px into the content. Text ranges drag natively.

question: Q4 per-container restriction
answer: No row/column drag in the open-source table package (no dragstart/DragDrop hits in ckeditor5-table, ckeditor5-list, ckeditor5-block-quote src); restrictions come from schema limits and canEditAt.

question: Q5 hover indicator and cost
answer: Every dragover runs findDropTargetRange (ancestor walk; when over a container gap it filters ALL children with getComputedStyle float check, then binary search with getBoundingClientRect); marker write throttled to 40ms, block line drawn by LineView.
